content.text: SKIP TO CONTENT inter Add to list ShareCopy link /ɪnˈtʌr/ /ˈɪntə/ IPA guide Other forms: interred; interring; inters Inter means to bury, usually in a tomb or grave. If you loved your cat a lot, you might want to inter her remains in the back yard and make a nice little memorial. Most of the time, the word inter is going to be about burying someone or something. Often times, a family owns a plot of land in a cemetery where all family members are interred when they die. Occasionally, you might see it in the phrase "inter alia," a literary Latin expression meaning "among other things." Your professor is probably a poet and a scholar, inter alia.
